clue.text: Leave out first part of Mitford's In Pursuit of Love

indicators.note: chasing behind, so the following piece comes after the letter for love

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, and a nil score looks like the letter O

indicators.note: only the opening stretch of the author's name is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A reader is told to skip the opening of Nancy Mitford's novel The Pursuit of Love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part of' takes MIT from the start of Mitford's, and 'In pursuit of' places it after O (love). Nancy Mitford's novel is really called The Pursuit of Love.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to skip or exclude it, a plain synonym for the verb phrase.

clue.text: Woman crazy about Bacchus enfin — they all are!

definitions.text: Woman crazy about Bacchus enfin — they all are!

indicators.note: the word for crazy goes around the woman's name

parts.note: crazy means mad
Ena is a woman's name, a common crossword stand-in for a woman

indicators.note: French for 'finally', so the god's name gives only its closing letter

explanation.surface: A woman besotted with the wine god, and the exclamation that all such women are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enfin' is French for 'finally'. The whole clue also describes the Bacchic women: every one of them was a woman crazy about the god.
explanation.definitionFit: The frenzied female followers of Dionysus, the Greek counterpart of Bacchus, were each a woman driven wild by the god.

clue.text: Great King, Gothic, rode about without a hint of gallantry

indicators.note: turned about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacking something, so a letter is taken away from the word Gothic
a hint gives just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A great Gothic monarch rides around with no trace of chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a hint of gallantry' removes G from Gothic, leaving OTHIC; 'about' then rearranges OTHIC with RODE. 'Gothic' looks like a description of the king, and he was indeed king of the Ostrogoths.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodoric the Great ruled the Ostrogoths and Italy around 500 AD, a monarch known by that epithet.

clue.text: Small room in a Midwest state close by where Poe kept his amontillado

parts.note: WI is the postal abbreviation for Wisconsin, a Midwestern US state

indicators.note: the small room goes inside the word for close by

parts.note: close by means near
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A tiny room near a Midwestern state, apparently the spot where Poe stored his sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: In Poe's tale The Cask of Amontillado, Montresor lures his victim down to the vaults with the promise of tasting a rare sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Poe's story the cask of sherry is supposedly stored in the underground wine store where Montresor walls up his rival.

clue.text: Remaining act in neglected play

parts.note: remaining somewhere is waiting there

indicators.note: the word for act goes inside the word for neglected

parts.note: neglected means forgot, as in forgot to do something
to act is to do

explanation.surface: A stage piece that has lingered, with an act in some forgotten drama.
explanation.walkthrough: This is Beckett's play, the theme of the puzzle. 'act' looks like part of a stage play, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's two-act drama about Vladimir and Estragon is a famous stage work.

clue.text: Lake seen in representation by Danish composer

indicators.note: a fresh representation of letters is a rearrangement of them

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A lake glimpsed in a picture painted by a composer from Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges L with the letters of SEEN IN. 'by' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen, writer of six symphonies, is Denmark's best-known classical composer.

clue.text: Nom de plume instrumental in the career of 26

definitions.text: Nom de plume instrumental in the career of 26

parts.words: Nom de plume instrumental in the career of 26
parts.note: a pen name used by the playwright at 26 when he wrote music criticism, which is also the Italian name of a musical instrument, so 'instrumental' has two senses

explanation.walkthrough: 26 is SHAW: George Bernard Shaw signed his London music reviews of the 1880s and 1890s with this Italian name for the basset horn.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw used the Italian term for the basset horn as his pen name as a music critic.

clue.text: One waiting for Miss Westenra about end of book

indicators.note: the first name goes around the final letter of book

parts.note: Lucy Westenra is the friend of Mina who becomes a vampire in Bram Stoker's Dracula

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone waits for Miss Westenra until the final page of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts K, the 'end of book', inside LUCY. Lucy Westenra is from Dracula; 'One waiting' points to the theme play.
explanation.definitionFit: Pozzo's slave in Beckett's play is one of the characters who wait in that drama.

clue.text: "There is no slander in an — fool, though he do nothing but rail"(Twelfth Night)

definitions.text: "There is no slander in an — fool, though he do nothing but rail"(Twelfth Night)

parts.words: "There is no slander in an — fool, though he do nothing but rail"(Twelfth Night)
parts.note: a quotation from Olivia in Twelfth Night with one word missing, the word that describes a licensed jester

explanation.walkthrough: Olivia tells Malvolio that a licensed fool may rail without it counting as slander; the missing word fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A permitted or licensed jester was called an 'allowed fool', free to mock without penalty.

clue.text: Little female seen in street at heart of Paris making comeback as opera coach

indicators.note: the word for little female is placed inside the reversed letters
coming back means the street word and the letter after it are read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street, fitting the Paris setting

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: petite is the French feminine for little, and describes a small woman

explanation.surface: A small woman spotted in a central Parisian street, returning as a coach for singers.
explanation.walkthrough: The French words fit the Paris setting. 'making comeback' turns the street and the heart letter together, and the little female then sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A répétiteur is a pianist who rehearses singers in their parts at an opera house.

clue.text: Old King depicted in eclogues, half mad

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters are shuffled
half of a word means only its first four letters here

explanation.surface: A monarch of old appears in pastoral poems, half insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes ECLO from ECLOGUES and 'mad' rearranges it. 'depicted in' only links. Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the English nursery rhyme, a legendary British ruler.

clue.text: Policemen — Irish ones to pull roughly back

indicators.note: the pieces are read in reverse order and backwards

parts.note: two words for one, I (the Roman numeral) and A
to drag something is to pull it roughly

explanation.surface: Irish officers asked to haul something roughly backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: IA and DRAG are read backwards because of 'back'. The plural of garda, the Irish word for a police officer, ends in -í.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the police force of the Irish Republic, and its officers are known by that name.

clue.text: Hedwig, say, gives distress call after taking cocaine

indicators.note: the cry comes after the drug slang in the answer

parts.note: snow is slang for cocaine
a yowl is a loud wail of distress

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's pet lets out a howl once it has snorted some coke.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedwig is Harry Potter's white owl in the J.K. Rowling books.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedwig, Harry Potter's pet in the J.K. Rowling books, is an example of the white Arctic bird.

clue.text: One waiting for notes to be rewritten about newspaper

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the word for newspaper
a rewritten word has its letters rearranged

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A man waits while his notes are redrafted around a newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rewritten' turns NOTES into ESTON, which goes 'about' RAG. Estragon is one of the two tramps who wait in Beckett's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Estragon is one of the two tramps who wait in Beckett's play.

clue.text: One enthusiastic with ecstasy, who's besotted by a sorrowful knight

definitions.text: who's besotted by a sorrowful knight

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
to be sold on something is to be enthusiastic about it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A keen person on ecstasy falls for a grieving knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces. The sorrowful knight is Tristan, whose doomed love is told in the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arthurian tale the Irish princess and the knight Tristan drink a love potion and are fatally devoted to each other.

clue.text: Adverse drug interactions may make one warm up so

indicators.note: suggests the letters can be worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Bad reactions between medicines might make someone feel warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges I (one) with the letters of WARM UP SO. 'Drug interactions' are the nineteenth-century conflicts between Britain and China over the opium trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain fought China twice in the 1800s over the opium trade, hostile dealings about a narcotic.

clue.text: Spanish infantry company I'll infiltrate in pursuit of small territory

indicators.note: following behind, so the company piece comes after the territory abbreviation

parts.note: Ter. is a short form of territory

indicators.note: to get inside something, so the letter goes into the abbreviation for company

parts.note: I'll is I will, so the letter I is what will infiltrate

explanation.surface: A Spanish army unit that a person plans to sneak into, chasing a little land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll' reads as 'I will', so the letter I is what will infiltrate. A tercio was a Spanish infantry formation of the 1500s and 1600s.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercio was a Spanish formation of pikemen and musketeers that dominated European battlefields in the 1500s.

clue.text: Retirees I become weary with, having chronic fatigue syndrome arising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to tire is to become weary
ME is the British name for chronic fatigue syndrome

explanation.surface: Someone says they grow tired along with a long-term exhaustion illness.
explanation.walkthrough: I, TIRE and ME are read upwards because of 'arising'. ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is the common British name for chronic fatigue syndrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus professors are those retired but keeping their title, so the Latin plural names retired people.

clue.text: Put in, in a word, for one waiting

definitions.meaning: joined into one word, the two clue words give the surname of the Russian president, whose first name is wanted
one of the two tramps who wait in Beckett's play

explanation.walkthrough: Write 'Put in' as one word and you have the Russian president's surname, and his first name is the answer. It is also the name of one of the waiting tramps in Beckett's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The president of Russia shares a first name with Didi, one of Beckett's tramps, so both readings name the same.

clue.text: Revolutionary comprehensive version of the Bible, that's plain

indicators.note: turning round, so the pieces that follow are read backwards in a down light

parts.note: all-in means comprehensive, as in an all-in price
AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible

explanation.surface: A revolutionary, inclusive version of scripture turns out to be ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses ALLIN plus AV. ALLIN is the British 'all-in', meaning comprehensive or inclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla in the figurative sense means ordinary or plain, having no special features.

clue.text: What features in one to tire badly?

definitions.text: What features in one to tire badly?

indicators.note: featuring something means having it inside, so the shuffled letters sit within the other two pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a means one

indicators.note: badly done, so the letters of tire are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about what afflicts someone who gets tired too easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes sluggishness, which is what a person who tires badly shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish resistance to moving or acting is the quality someone shows when they are weary and lethargic.

clue.text: Latter-day heathen composing no paean about God initially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the first letter of God
making up, so the letters are put together in a new order
initially means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A modern pagan writes no hymn of praise to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' rearranges NO PAEAN, which goes 'about' G, the first letter of God ('initially').
explanation.definitionFit: A neopagan follows a revived pre-Christian religion, a modern heathen.

clue.text: One waiting for quiet Australian going on and coming back

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, quiet
Oz is slang for Australia, so Australian gives OZ

indicators.note: returning means the Australian slang is read backwards the second time

parts.note: Oz again, the second time read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone waits for a quiet Aussie who keeps leaving and returning.
explanation.walkthrough: OZ appears 'going on' (forwards) and 'coming back' (reversed). Pozzo is the bullying master of Lucky in Beckett's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Pozzo, Lucky's master, is one of the characters in Beckett's play about waiting.

clue.text: Smiles caused by translation of Maus by English lecturer

indicators.note: translating reworks a word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grins provoked by an English academic's version of Art Spiegelman's Maus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges MAUS, then E and L follow. 'caused by' and 'by' link. Samuel Smiles was the Victorian author of Self-Help.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Smiles, the Scottish author of Self-Help (1859), is identified here by his surname, so the clue wants his first name.

clue.text: Vivacity of Hablot Knight Browne, we hear

indicators.note: says the illustrator's pen name is to be spoken rather than read

parts.note: Phiz was the pen name of Hablot Knight Browne, illustrator of Dickens

explanation.surface: The liveliness of a Victorian illustrator, by all reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Hablot Knight Browne signed his illustrations for Dickens's novels as Phiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizz means sparkle or liveliness, a lively zest.

clue.text: I heard no longer / The snowy-banded, -, / Delicate-handed priest intone (Tennyson)

definitions.text: I heard no longer / The snowy-banded, -, / Delicate-handed priest intone (Tennyson)

parts.words: I heard no longer / The snowy-banded, -, / Delicate-handed priest intone (Tennyson)
parts.note: a quotation from Tennyson's poem The Daisy with one word missing, describing the priest as an amateur dabbler

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word comes from Tennyson's The Daisy, recalling a dainty priest heard chanting in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler or amateur dandy is the sense Tennyson gives the priest in that line.

clue.text: Note Greek maiden embracing missing deserter, lovestruck in Boccaccio poem

parts.note: F is a musical note

indicators.note: the maiden's name wraps around the other two pieces

parts.note: Io was the maiden loved by Zeus in Greek myth
lost means missing
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A musical note and a Greek girl hugging an absent turncoat, all smitten in an Italian poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Boccaccio's Il Filostrato, whose title roughly means 'laid low by love', was the source of Chaucer's Troilus and Criseyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's poem title is usually glossed as 'one prostrated by love', so it means overcome by love.

clue.text: Old relative of 6 losing first of matches for GB

indicators.note: dropping, so a letter is removed from the old instrument

parts.note: the shawm is an old reed instrument, a relation of the basset horn at 6

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An elderly family member of a player loses the first game played for Great Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAWM loses M (the 'first of matches'). The basset horn at 6 is a woodwind, and GB stands for George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw is known by his initials, GBS, so GB points to his surname.
